headline: Markets steady after Nvidia's leadership shock as AI-bubble debate simmers
body: Equities closed lower Thursday for a second straight session, with the Nasdaq off 0.39% to 25,366, the S&P 500 down 0.35% to 7,592, and the Dow slipping 0.36% to 52,297. The proximate trigger was Nvidia, where CEO Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately following a board inquiry tied to a personal-conduct matter with national-security overtones; CFO Colette Kress stepped in as interim chief and the board named its first independent chair. Nvidia shares have been under pressure since the board disclosed the investigation on November 8, and options markets are pricing real uncertainty into the stock ahead of its November 17 earnings. Even so, the pullback looks more like digestion than panic: the 10-year yield closed above 5% and the VIX ticked up to 18.70, levels that read as cautious rather than stressed, and both the Nasdaq and S&P 500 remain on pace for solid weekly gains after bouncing off the sharper early-November AI-stock selloff.

The bigger backdrop is a live debate over AI-spending sustainability rather than any single stock. Hyperscaler capex guidance near $735 billion for 2026 — up roughly 79% from last year — has investors weighing whether demand can keep pace with the buildout, a question sharpened by commentary from figures such as Goldman Sachs' CEO flagging a possible 10-20% market drawdown and the Bank of England's governor openly raising bubble language. Cross-asset signals are mixed rather than uniformly risk-off: oil rallied while gold slid to its lowest level in over a year, not the classic flight-to-safety pattern. Retail-sentiment chatter on the Nvidia leadership change was present but not dominant in today's search results, so this read leans more on price action and institutional commentary than on a clear social-media mood signal; the AI-bubble argument, more than meme-stock enthusiasm, is what's holding retail attention right now.
